stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Four slots form a series loop. Drag components from the palette to build a working circuit and place the ammeter to read the current $I$ (in mA). Move the ammeter to two different slots and confirm the reading is the same — current is conserved around a series loop.
stages.concept: Electric current $I$ measures the rate at which charge crosses a section: $I = \Delta Q / \Delta t$, in amperes ($1\,\text{A} = 1\,\text{C/s}$). In a series loop, $I$ is the same at every point — an ammeter reads the same value no matter where it sits in the loop.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Two targets. Insert the ammeter into the loop and choose the right dipoles so the reading matches each target current in turn. Adding a resistor drops the current; removing it restores the full value.
stages.concept: The intensity $I$ of the current is set by the source and by what the circuit contains. For a given battery, a larger total resistance means a smaller $I$. The ammeter, wired in series, does not perturb the loop — it only reports.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Three slots are pre-placed. One is empty. Pick the single component that satisfies the goal shown in the corner and drop it in — one attempt. The ammeter reading stays hidden until you commit.
stages.concept: Before touching the palette, reason on paper: is the loop already closed? Is there a receiver? Do we need to measure, complete, or receive current? Then commit.

labels.goal_measure: add a device that measures I without changing the circuit
labels.goal_receive: add the receiver so current can flow
labels.goal_close: close the loop without changing the ammeter reading
labels.diag_no_battery: no source — nothing drives the current
labels.diag_no_ammeter: loop closed — drop the ammeter in to read I
labels.tip1: drag from the palette; drag a placed component out to remove it; the ammeter shows I in mA
labels.tip2: the ammeter must be in the loop for the reading to count — swap resistors to change I
labels.tip3: read the goal, reason on paper, then place one component
labels.peek_tip: The intensity I is the same at every point of a series loop. Ask what the goal really needs: a measuring device (ammeter), a receiver (lamp), or a plain conductor (wire)?

1.1: Start by dragging four components onto the four slots so a lamp lights.
1.2: Put the ammeter into one of the empty slots and read the number that appears above it.
1.3: Move the ammeter to a second slot in the same loop. The reading should not change — that is what 'I is uniform' means.

2.1: Only readings taken with the ammeter actually in the loop count toward a target.
2.2: The full-lit current is 240 mA. Adding a single resistor drops it to 60 mA.
2.3: For target 240 mA: battery + wire + lamp + ammeter. For target 60 mA: battery + resistor + lamp + ammeter.

3.1: Read the goal chip in the top-right corner. It tells you what role the missing component must play.
3.2: A wire completes a loop without adding resistance. An ammeter measures I. A lamp is a receiver. A resistor lowers I.
3.3: Match the missing role to the goal: 'measure I' → ammeter, 'receiver' → lamp, 'close the loop' → wire.
